newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley expects benefits in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley expects benefits in 2nd half.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co said Wednesday it expects to reap the benefits of restructuring efforts in the second half of 1997.

The printing and information technology company reported a first-quarter profit of $29.3 million or $0.20 per share. A year ago, it had a loss of $376.9 million or $2.45 per share, which included a $512 million pre-tax restructuring charge.
Excluding the charge, net income for the 1996 quarter was $34 million or $0.22 per share.
"We are progressing well on the restructuring actions previously announced, and we expect the benefits from those actions to begin to flow during the second half," said chairman William Davis.
"We will continue to rigorously evaluate costs and carefully manage capital and cash flow in every area of the company to increase shareholder value," Davis added in a statement.
The executive said demand in many of Donnelley's businesses -- notably books and financial printing -- improved during the first quarter.
